subtitle: Private mental health tools.
description:
Selftend is a set of free, private mental health tools: everyday tools for right now, and a CBT programme — cognitive behavioural therapy — to work through when you want one.

It is not a therapist and not a diagnosis engine. It is a place to write things down, notice patterns, and work through them with structured exercises drawn from CBT and ACT.

What is inside

- Journalling and a gratitude log
- CBT thought records, with a guided walkthrough
- Mood, sleep, and activity tracking
- Breathing, grounding, and meditation exercises
- ACT tools: values, defusion, expansion, committed action
- Routines and habits, if you want them

How it works

Pick the parts you want. Nothing is compulsory, and modules you do not enable stay out of your way. Reminders are off unless you turn them on, and quiet by default when you do.

Your writing is yours

Entries are encrypted at rest. Selftend has no ads, no trackers, and no analytics SDKs. It does not sell anything and there is nothing to upgrade to.

Free, and open source

Selftend is free to use and the source is public. It is built as a non-profit project.

If you are in crisis, Selftend is not the right tool. In-app crisis guidance points to real services.
promoText: Free and open source. Journalling, CBT thought records, mood and sleep tracking, breathing and grounding - the tools are yours to pick from, at whatever pace suits you.
